fixture: Integrator input-sampling bench (issue #106): the full integrator cell + ota_fd clocked for 6 complete phi1/phi2 cycles; the differential charge the input pass gate `Sin` delivered onto Csi, read at the instant phi1e falls and the sample is frozen
result_kind: simulated (ngspice, transistor-level netlists of design/integrator + design/ota/ota_fd; not the behavioural model). SIMULATED, NEVER MEASURED.
assembled_from: cached .partials/ (fleet results from an earlier invocation; nothing was submitted for this record)

conditions.phi1_duration_note: the input path has 90.4 ns: phi1 closes Sin at 0.1 ns into the cycle and phi1e opens Sci at 90.5 ns, which is when the charge on Csi is frozen. phi1 itself stays closed to 92.5 ns, but that moves both plates of Csi together and cannot change the sampled charge.
conditions.which_reading_is_the_headline: sampled_V (across Csi). What phi2 transfers onto Ci is the charge stored on Csi, which is Cs times the ACROSS-plate voltage at the phi1e fall. At a slow/cold corner Sci is resistive too, so the top plates are not exactly at vcm then and the bottom-plate-only reading (sampled_bpi_only_V) is larger by exactly the top-plate differential -- at ss/1.620V/-40C and the 0.2 V amplitude, 0.0991 V against 0.0914 V. The across-plate reading is the one that matches the per-clock output step issue #106 reported, so error_rel is computed from it; error_rel_bpi_only is carried alongside.
conditions.measured_quantity: samp_s<k> = the differential voltage across Csi, (bpi_p - tpi_p) - (bpi_n - tpi_n), as a mean over the last 0.8 ns of phi1e in cycle k. Do NOT read this as equal to v(xint.bpi_p) - v(xint.bpi_n): that equality holds only while Sci still pins both top plates to vcm at the phi1e fall, which is true to the reported precision over most of the grid but false at the slow/cold corners -- at fs/1.620V/-40C and the 0.6 V amplitude the two forms differ by 78.9 mV. The bottom-plate-only form is carried alongside as sampled_bpi_only_V and their difference as top_plate_differential_V; which_reading_is_the_headline says which one error_rel uses.
conditions.reset: bench-only ideal 1 ohm switches across Ci until 40 ns (cell has none)
conditions.clocks: behavioural rail-to-rail on Vdda from PULSE shape sources, 200 ps edges, >= 4.7 ns non-overlap, no non-overlap generator
conditions.load_per_side: 0.1 pF output parasitics only (integrator 1, case B of design/integrator/SIZING.md)
conditions.spice_options: reltol=1e-5 vntol=1e-7 abstol=1e-13 chgtol=1e-16 (in the deck)
conditions.dac: held at VCM, dn static: the reference branch transfers zero charge while all of its switches still operate and inject

post_v0p2.note: shipped cell, +0.2 V differential input, DAC nulled: signal dependence

post_v0p6.note: shipped cell, +0.6 V differential input (vinp/vinn = 1.2/0.6 V), DAC nulled: the large-signal end of the issue #106 input-sampling sweep. With the DAC nulled nothing cancels the input, so the differential output ramps 0.3 V per clock and leaves the OTA's range before the last cycle. That is accepted deliberately: the sampled charge is set on Csi while Sci holds the top plate at vcm and Sti is open, so the bottom-plate measurement does not depend on the output, and no output number from this variant is read or reported.

conditions.switch_under_test: XSin_<p,n>_n = sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 W 4 / L 0.15 in parallel with XSin_<p,n>_p = sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 W 8 / L 0.15, gated by phi1/phi1b -- a complementary pass gate with no low-Vth half. Its DC Ron versus the voltage it passes is sim/switch-probe/probe-i106.json.

corner_set: DR-002 full grid, 5 process x 3 T x 3 Vdda, per amplitude
pass_criterion: NONE. This is an extraction, not a spec check. No measurement in either request carries a limit, and no ratified spec row bounds input-sampling completeness -- so this record states none, relaxes none, and adds none. The `pass` field below means only that every corner simulated without erroring; it is not a verdict on the circuit. The error is reported against a labelled reference line (derived.reference_line_label), which is a scale and not a threshold. No SNDR, ENOB or resolution consequence is claimed or implied: nothing here has been through model B.

input_level_dependence.note: error_rel at the two amplitudes, corner by corner. Equal fractions would be a pure gain error; a difference is a level-dependent error, i.e. distortion. This bench measures the difference, it does not convert it into a distortion or SNDR figure -- nothing here has been through model B.
